arxiv-1911-08924.title: Geometric Planar Networks on Bichromatic Collinear Points Thanks: A preliminary version of this paper appeared in the proceedings of 6th Annual International Conference on Algorithms and Discrete Applied Mathematics (CALDAM 2020), and the full version appeared in the Theoretical Computer Science (TC
arxiv-1911-08924.creator: Sayan Bandyapadhyay, Aritra Banik, Sujoy Bhore, Martin Nöllenburg
arxiv-1911-08924.description: Abstract We study three classical graph problems – Hamiltonian path, minimum spanning tree, and minimum perfect matching on geometric graphs induced by bichromatic (red and blue) points. These problems have been widely studied for points in the Euclidean plane, and many of them are 𝖭𝖯 \mathsf{NP} -hard. In this work, we consider these problems for collinear points.

arxiv-2202-12525.title: Embedded Soft Sensing in Soft Ring Actuator for Aiding with the Self-Organisation of the In-Hand Rotational Manipulation
arxiv-2202-12525.creator: Ryman Hashem, Fumiya Iida
arxiv-2202-12525.description: Abstract This paper proposes a soft sensor embedded in a soft ring actuator with five fingers as a soft hand to identify the bifurcation of manipulated objects during the in-hand manipulation process. The manipulation is performed by breaking the symmetry method with an underactuated control system by bifurcating the object to clockwise or counter-clockwise rotations.

arxiv-2211-03211.title: Towards real-time 6D pose estimation of objects in single-view cone-beam X-ray
arxiv-2211-03211.creator: Christiaan G.A. Viviers, Joël de Bruijn, Lena Filatova, Peter H.N. de With, Fons van der Sommen
arxiv-2211-03211.description: Abstract Deep learning-based pose estimation algorithms can successfully estimate the pose of objects in an image, especially in the field of color images. 6D Object pose estimation based on deep learning models for X-ray images often use custom architectures that employ extensive CAD models and simulated data for training purposes.

arxiv-2507-22586.title: Random matrix theory of charge distribution in disordered quantum impurity models
arxiv-2507-22586.creator: Maxime Debertolis, Serge Florens
arxiv-2507-22586.description: Abstract We introduce a bare-bone random matrix quantum impurity model, by hybridizing a localized spinless electronic level with a bath of random fermions in the Gaussian Orthogonal Ensemble (GOE). While stripped out of correlations effects, this model reproduces some salient features of the impurity charge distribution obtained in previous works on interacting disordered impurity models.

arxiv-2510-10033.creator: Sebastian Gant and Ben Williams
arxiv-2510-10033.description: Abstract . Working over an algebraically closed field of characteristic 0 0 , we show that the motivic stable homotopy groups of the sphere spectrum can be determined entirely from the motivic homotopy groups of the p p -completed sphere spectra and the motivic cohomology of the ground field, except possibly for the 0 0 and − 1 -1 -stems.

pmc-10546163.creator: Andrew McCarthy, Dilupa Samarakoon, Joanne Gray, Peter Mcmeekin, Stephen McCarthy, Claire Newton, Marielle Nobbenhuis, Jonathan Lippiatt, Jeremy Twigg

pmc-11575025.title: Enhancing puncture skills training with generative AI and digital technologies: a parallel cohort study
pmc-11575025.creator: Zhe Ji, Yuliang Jiang, Haitao Sun, Bin Qiu, Yi Chen, Mao Li, Jinghong Fan, Junjie Wang
pmc-11575025.description: BackgroundTraditional puncture skills training for refresher doctors faces limitations in effectiveness and efficiency. This study explored the application of generative AI (ChatGPT), templates, and digital imaging to enhance puncture skills training.Methods90 refresher doctors were enrolled sequentially into 3 groups: traditional training; template and digital imaging training; and ChatGPT, template and digital imaging training.

pmc-11716150.title: Worry differentially affects the impact of placental growth factor on processing speed in older adults with amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment
pmc-11716150.creator: Jovian C Lam, Adriana Savettiere, Peter Louras, Jennifer Kaci Fairchild
pmc-11716150.description: BackgroundPlacental growth factor (PIGF) is an angiogenic, pro‐inflammatory biomarker that is overexpressed in cardiovascular diseases. Recent literature has linked PIGF to the identification of cognitive impairment with white matter burden. Worry is associated with an increased risk for cardiovascular disease, accelerated aging and subsequent reduced brain volume, and decline in cognition.
